descriptionChirho: The Roman province of Syria, a geographic region north of Palestine that included the city of Antioch, a major center of early Christianity; mentioned in contexts of Jesus' fame spreading (Matt 4:24), Roman governance (Luke 2:2), and Paul's missionary journeys (Acts 15:23, 41; 18:18; 20:3; 21:3; Gal 1:21). Both clusters are the same proper noun with minor orthographic variation in transliteration. Spanish 'Siria/Syría' shows the classical vs modern spelling variation; Hindi 'सीरिया/सुरिया' reflects two transliteration traditions; Arabic 'سُورِيَّة/سورِيَة' (with and without shadda) are trivial orthographic variants of the same name; Korean '수리아' is uniform across both clusters; Swahili alternates between 'Siria', 'Shamu' (from Sham, the Arabic regional name), and 'Suría', revealing rich cultural naming layers.
